paragraphs: The Vario 511D was part of the Vario commercial range from 1996 to 2013, sitting within the lighter chassis bracket alongside the 508D, 510D and 512D. It used either the OM602 2.9-litre diesel or the later OM611 2.2-litre diesel, depending on the exact production period. Both engines are shared with the equivalent-era Sprinter range, which means the known wear patterns - timing chain, timing gear and injector seal wear - are well understood and consistent across both units. The Vario was discontinued in 2013, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every VARIO 511D on the road.

cards.body: A 2.9-litre inline-five diesel fitted to the Vario 511D across the 1996-2013 production run. Known for timing chain, timing gear and injector seal wear - see the callout above. We replace timing chains, timing gears, injector seals and gaskets as standard on every OM602 rebuild.

A 2.2-litre inline-four diesel fitted to the Vario 511D across the 1996-2013 production run. Shares the same known wear pattern as the OM602 - timing chain, timing gear and injector seal wear - and we replace the same components as standard on every OM611 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: The Vario 511D spans two engine options across its production run - the 2.9L OM602 and the 2.2L OM611. Fitting the wrong replacement - or assuming parts from one engine will fit the other - risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic Vario quote - it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
